title: Use cases supported by Personalisation Hub
summary: The 3 primary use cases — connected retail experience, first-party retail media targeting and hyper-localised QSR campaigns — with links to the articles that set each up.
bodyMd:
Personalisation Hub supports 3 primary use cases: a connected and personalised retail experience, first-party audience targeting in-store and hyper-localised campaigns. This page describes each scenario and links to the articles that set it up. For the sector view, see Benefits by industry.

Core platform features

All 3 use cases build on the same features. The platform runs entirely within your own AWS account and private VPC — see Where is my data stored and how is the platform secured?.


Use case 1: connected and personalised retail experience

Applies to telco, banking and brick-and-mortar retail. The visitor's phone, the store's displays and the staff tablet support a connected retail experience for every customer visit.

Virtual queues and appointments


Connected customer journeys


Dynamic QR code engagement


Staff tablet


Intended outcomes. Shorter perceived wait times, better-informed conversations with staff, a connected experience between onsite and in-store, and conversion and retention that can be measured in your respective analytics/insights solution(s).

Use case 2: first-party audience targeting in-store (e.g. for retail media)

Uses loyalty and other customer or decisioning data to target in-store campaigns as support for third-party cookies decline.

Automatic store check-in


Connected customer journeys


QR code store check-in


Programmatic advertising slots (coming soon)

Localised, personalised and sponsored ad slots that a brand designates for advertisers, bookable in advance or filled programmatically, with DSP integrations planned. This capability is on the roadmap and is not in the platform today.

Intended outcomes. Larger baskets and higher conversion, monetisation of in-store media, closed-loop attribution through the Downloads reports, and the ability to change a campaign in real time. See Review campaign performance in Insights / Analytics.

Use case 3: hyper-localised campaigns for quick-service restaurants

Quick-service restaurants integrate local data to control how menus and offers are presented.

Day-parting (advanced scheduling)


Dynamic data integration


Personalised offers


Vision at the edge (audience sensing)


Intended outcomes. Higher sales per visit, less manual menu maintenance, more engagement with offers, campaign decisions based on playback and audience data, and less waste from promoting items that are out of stock.
